column3: Build both collision quadtrees: los_build_tree(0x1000) -> g_los_tree_a (sight-blocking features), los_build_tree(0x0100) -> g_los_tree_b
Allocate a 5000-byte block, build a quadtree of the world objects matching the flag mask with los_build_node, shrink the block to the used size; returns its segment (near)
Free both quadtree blocks and zero g_los_tree_a/b
Coarse reject: object centre +- (model radius) vs the endpoints +- query radius, compared on the high 16 bits per axis; CF=1 = may overlap (near)

Segment query (pascal: ignore obj, from, to, radius, hit out, mask, include-flagged, test ground, test dynamic list, unused): tests objects of the two endpoint leaves, the dynamic list and the ground; returns hit object, 0xFFFF for ground, or 0
Cohen-Sutherland 6-bit outcode of local point p1 against the grown model box (near)
Cohen-Sutherland 6-bit outcode of local point p2 (near)
Sample the model heightmap at local (x,z); CF=1 if y <= surface height, then p1 = (x, h, z) (near pascal)
Test clipped p1, the midpoint and p2 against the model heightmap; CF=1 on the first hit (near)
Rotate the (x,z) of p1 and p2 by -AX around (0,0) with 2255:62D0 (near)

Precise object test: transform the segment into model space (heading), clip it against the model box grown by the radius (Cohen-Sutherland, max 15 steps), optional heightmap test, write the world hit point; CF=1 hit (near)
Ground plane y=0 test (y<0 underground): writes the crossing point; CF=1 hit (near)
Walk a quadtree leaf's zero-terminated object list and return the first object hit (containers recurse into their child list) or 0 (near)
Same filtering and testing over a linked object list (next at +4); recursive for containers (near)
Descend the quadtree in DS from node 0 by (x_hi >= midX) + 2*(z_hi >= midZ) (unsigned) to a leaf; returns its offset (near)
Recursive quadtree node builder over (xmin,zmin,xmax,zmax) in high-16 units: leaf with up to 9 objects, else 4 children split at the midpoints (near)
